day-85-act-01.title: Capstone Charter: Problem, User, and Bounded Scope
day-85-act-01.prerequisites: Days 82-84 scientific agent evaluation; the bounded agent Learning Project at projects/agent_learning and its four-language guides.
day-85-act-01.objective: Author a one-page capstone charter that binds a concrete problem, a named user, an explicit scope boundary, and non-goals, reusing the previously verified bounded agent rather than hiding a new unbounded system inside the capstone.
day-85-act-01.instructions:
1. Re-read projects/agent_learning/README.md and agent.py; list the registered bounded tools (list_notes, read_note, write_report) and the fixture task summarize-notes.
2. Write the problem statement: the capstone extends the verified notes-to-report agent with exactly one new bounded tool (for example count_words or list_deadlines) and one additional fixed task, still scored by the existing independent scorer.
3. Name the user (a learner assembling study notes into a report) and the usage context (a local, offline-first disposable fixture workspace).
4. Draw the scope line. IN: the deterministic adapter, registered bounded tools, fixed fixtures, step/retry budgets. OUT: open-web browsing, arbitrary shell execution, unbounded retries, production autonomy.
5. Declare non-goals: no live-model claims until the ticket-23 authorization gate is approved; no new agent framework; no hidden network calls.
6. Save the draft as capstone_charter.md.
day-85-act-01.exercise_prompt: Draft capstone_charter.md with sections Problem, User, In-Scope, Out-of-Scope, and Non-Goals. Then classify three feature requests as in-scope or out-of-scope: (a) 'read a third note from the fixture', (b) 'let the agent pip-install any package it wants', (c) 'add a bounded word-count tool'.
day-85-act-01.hint: Ask whether the feature crosses a resource or permission boundary already enforced by agent.py; (a) and (c) stay inside the fixture, while (b) grants unbounded execution.
day-85-act-01.answer: Reference ruling: (a) in-scope (fixture change only); (b) out-of-scope (arbitrary package installs are unbounded execution); (c) in-scope (one bounded deterministic tool). A charter is acceptable only when every in-scope item maps to an existing bound - a registered tool, a fixture, or a budget - and the non-goals name at least three excluded capabilities.
day-85-act-01.mastery_criterion: Produce a charter whose every in-scope item maps to a stated bound and whose non-goals explicitly exclude at least three capabilities (e.g., web browsing, arbitrary code execution, unbounded retries).

day-85-act-02.title: Acceptance Contract: Fixed Tasks, Baseline, and Ceilings
day-85-act-02.prerequisites: Day 85 Activity 1 charter draft; the ticket-23 contract schema in projects/agent_learning/evidence/live_eval_contract.json.
day-85-act-02.objective: Convert the charter into a measurable acceptance contract: a fixed task set, the deterministic baseline and its report hash, metric definitions, resource ceilings, failure cases, and the exact submission evidence a reviewer will inspect.
day-85-act-02.instructions:
1. Copy the schema style of projects/agent_learning/evidence/live_eval_contract.json and create capstone_acceptance.json.
2. Bind the task set: keep the six live-eval task categories (success, two malformed tool requests, missing input, loop, budget exhaustion) and add the one new fixed task from the charter; freeze it before any tuning.
3. Record the baseline: adapter deterministic-v1, fixture summarize-notes, expected_report_sha256 9e8315034af750009a4b2cfb261a077428afe441bc45c602cb7ead32ac0fd787, plus the baseline command python -m projects.agent_learning.cli evaluate --fixture summarize-notes --output <path>.
4. Define metrics per task: status, steps, retries, termination reason, and report-hash equality, mirroring the contract's scorer dimensions (outcome, tool behavior, budget, failure handling).
5. Set resource ceilings: max 6 steps per task, max 2 retries per fault, a 30-minute runtime ceiling, a USD 5.00 cost ceiling for any authorized live run, and stop conditions copied from the contract.
6. List submission evidence: charter, this contract, the baseline ledger, per-task results, the failure log, and the provenance table.
day-85-act-02.exercise_prompt: Write capstone_acceptance.json containing all nine required elements - problem, user, scope, model_choice, baseline, evaluation_set, failure_cases, resource_limits, submission_evidence - with live-run fields explicitly null and labeled not-run-awaiting-authorization.
day-85-act-02.hint: Predeclare direction only, like the LoRA comparison contract: aim for 'deterministic-baseline parity without unbounded steps' rather than a promised improvement percentage.
day-85-act-02.answer: A valid contract has every field populated or an explicitly gated null, the baseline bound by fixture hash and command, and checkable success criteria: for example 6/6 deterministic tasks pass within the step budget and malformed requests produce structured errors rather than crashes.
day-85-act-02.mastery_criterion: Produce a contract under which a reviewer can predict pass/fail for each task before any run; live-run fields stay null and carry the not-run-awaiting-authorization label.

day-85-act-03.title: Model Selection: Trained Adapters vs Existing Models
day-85-act-03.prerequisites: Day 85 Activities 1-2; the ticket-19 evidence package and the ticket-21 LoRA comparison contract.
day-85-act-03.objective: Decide which model powers the capstone agent by inspecting the cloud pretraining evidence package and the LoRA comparison contract, while keeping an appropriate existing model admissible when it performs better for the final agent.
day-85-act-03.instructions:
1. Open curriculum/projects/docs/pretrain-cloud-evidence/evidence-package.json: note the 4-layer/4-head/64-embedding GPT recipe, the tinyshakespeare data provenance and SHA-256, and run_status=blocked - the pretraining work teaches the data-to-checkpoint loop but yields no production-capable model.
2. Open projects/lora/evidence/comparison_contract.json: note base_model openai-community/gpt2, LoRA r=8 alpha=16 on q_proj/v_proj, seed 42 splits 0.8/0.1/0.1, status=blocked-awaiting-authorization, and success criteria that predeclare direction only.
3. Read projects/agent_learning/evidence/model_selection_plan.md: one open-weight local candidate recommended plus three provider API alternatives, each with version, access, data-usage, and cost conditions.
4. Build the decision table. Candidates: (a) self-trained GPT from the pretraining recipe, (b) the LoRA-adapted gpt2, (c) the recommended existing open model. Score each on observed evidence, not aspiration: deterministic-baseline parity, license and redistribution rights, pinned revisions, and cost ceilings.
5. Record the decision honestly: the deterministic-v1 adapter remains the offline evaluation baseline; for any authorized live run the recommended open-weight model is admissible because self-trained artifacts are unproven - pretraining and LoRA results inform the design without obliging their use.
6. Save the analysis as model_decision.md with one license row per candidate.
day-85-act-03.exercise_prompt: Produce model_decision.md: a three-row candidate table (evidence file, license, verdict) plus a one-paragraph rationale naming the chosen live-run candidate and explaining why the self-trained options inform but do not drive the final agent.
day-85-act-03.hint: A blocked run_status is evidence of a controlled process, not of model quality; cite what each artifact actually proves.
day-85-act-03.answer: Reference verdict: the live-run candidate is the recommended open-weight local model (pinned revision recorded in the selection plan, license reviewed) because the pretraining artifact documents a learning recipe and the LoRA contract is blocked-awaiting-authorization; deterministic-v1 remains the checked baseline. Choosing an existing model is correct engineering, not a shortcut, when it performs better.
day-85-act-03.mastery_criterion: Justify the model choice with citations to all three evidence artifacts, a license check per candidate, and zero invented measurements.

day-85-act-04.title: Assessment: Charter Review Gate and Scope Freeze
day-85-act-04.objective: Run a structured go/no-go review of the charter and acceptance contract against a fixed nine-element checklist, freeze scope, and write the recovery plan for any failed element.
day-85-act-04.instructions:
1. Assemble the nine-element checklist: concrete problem, named user, scope boundary, model choice, baseline, evaluation set, failure cases, resource limits, submission evidence.
2. Score the charter and contract element by element; each element is PRESENT or MISSING with a one-line pointer to where it is defined.
3. If every element is present, freeze scope: record scope_frozen=true and the freeze date; later feature requests must route through re-review.
4. If any element is missing, write a NO-GO verdict naming the missing elements and the specific activity (act-01, act-02, or act-03) that repairs it.
5. Dry-run one scope-creep request ('add a chat UI') and show it fails the scope line.
6. Save the signed review as charter_review.json.
day-85-act-04.exercise_prompt: Produce charter_review.json: nine checklist verdicts with evidence pointers, a final GO or NO-GO, and - regardless of verdict - the scope-creep ruling for 'add a chat UI'.
day-85-act-04.hint: A pointer is a file path plus a section, such as capstone_charter.md#Non-Goals; 'in my head' is not evidence.
day-85-act-04.answer: GO requires 9/9 PRESENT. 'Add a chat UI' is out-of-scope: it is a new delivery surface not bound by the harness budgets and must wait for a separately scoped project.
day-85-act-04.mastery_criterion: Complete a review gate where every verdict cites stored evidence and the scope-freeze or NO-GO decision is explicit and reproducible.
